subject: Human Body
title: The Parathyroid and Calcium
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Parathyroid and Calcium.

hook.text: Four tiny glands behind your thyroid control calcium levels. Calcium is essential for heartbeat, muscles, and nerves.

buildup.text: PTH raises blood calcium by pulling it from bones, boosting gut absorption, and reducing kidney excretion.

discovery.text: Calcitonin from the thyroid does the opposite: it lowers calcium by depositing it into bones when levels rise too high.

twist.text: If parathyroids are accidentally removed during thyroid surgery, calcium crashes. Muscles spasm uncontrollably.

climax.text: Calcium balance matters far beyond bones. Your heart, muscles, and nerves all depend on parathyroid precision.

punchline.text: Four glands the size of rice grains keep your heart beating.

quiz.question: What happens if parathyroid glands are removed?
options: Blood calcium drops dangerously, causing muscle spasms
Bone density increases until they become brittle
